headline: The gold requires freezing three stolen cards and then unfreezing them before closing, but the policy says to recommend closing instead of freezing once a theft is confirmed, and skipping the freeze changes the graded state.

issues.summary: The customer opens by saying the wallet was stolen an hour ago. Doc_..._026 tells the agent to recommend closing rather than freezing for a confirmed lost or stolen card. The gold instead freezes all three cards, unfreezes them, and then closes them. The freeze and unfreeze leave timestamps and tool-log rows that a direct-close path never writes.
evidence: user_scenario step 1: "Hi, my wallet was stolen about an hour ago and I need to freeze all my debit cards immediately."
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026: "CLOSE: Permanent deactivation - cannot be reversed. Use when card is confirmed lost/stolen"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026: "If customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing"
gold[4..6] freeze_debit_card_3892 on dbc_cr89a2b3c4_ev/_lb/_green; gold[13..15] unfreeze_debit_card_3893 on the same cards; gold[17..19] close_debit_card_4721 reason 'stolen'

Replay (snapshot env): gold minus the freeze/unfreeze calls -> agent/user hash mismatch; diff = frozen_date and unfrozen_date '11/14/2025' on all three cards plus agent_discoverable_tools rows for freeze_debit_card_3892 and unfreeze_debit_card_3893
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that follows doc_..._026 and closes the stolen cards directly ends in the same business state (three closed cards, Evergreen and Green reordered, Light Blue waiting 48 hours) but fails the exact DB hash. Only the agent that follows the customer's literal freeze request passes.
issues.suggested_fix: Have the customer ask to cancel the cards rather than freeze them, and drop gold[3..6] and gold[12..15]. Alternatively, keep the freeze-first story but make the opening uncertain ('I think my wallet may have been stolen') so freezing is the policy-preferred first step.

solution_check: Reconstructed: verify, list accounts, read transactions (chk_cr89a2b3c4_3 has a pending REFUND, which doc_..._025 requirement 5 lets the customer waive by acknowledgment), close all three cards as 'stolen'. Order Evergreen (PREMIUM, doc_..._005) with RUSH delivery_fee 35 and PREMIUM design_fee 0, and Green (MID) with STANDARD/CLASSIC at 0/0. Light Blue (ENTRY, 2 replacements in 12 months: 08/10/2025 and 04/05/2025) is closed but not reordered because of the ENTRY 48-hour wait, even though the $25 fee is accepted. The orders and closures match gold[17..24]; the freeze/unfreeze prefix is the only divergence risk.
prior_note: The prior review rated this task clean under a relaxed scorer. Under exact-hash grading, the freeze/unfreeze timestamps make the gold path-dependent.
notes: The pending refund (btxn_d0b8b00ed468, type 'refund', status 'pending') is also a pending transaction under doc_..._025 requirement 4, which would block closure. The gold applies the refund-specific waiver in requirement 5; specific-over-general supports that, but it is an ambiguity a verifier may want to weigh. No credit cards exist for cr89a2b3c4. Light Blue reorder: the excess-fee acceptance plus the 48-hour wait means no order, consistent with doc_..._029.
